name: Grade 6 T1: Internet Addresses and Packets
description: Internet addresses, domain names, DNS, IP addresses, packets, headers, payloads, and data transfer.

words.definition: A label that helps computers find a device, website, or place online.
words.example: A website address tells the browser where to go.

words.definition: The readable name of a website, such as example.com.
words.example: The domain helps people remember a website more easily than numbers.

words.definition: The system that matches a domain name to the IP address a computer needs.
words.example: DNS works like a phone book for websites.

words.definition: A number-based address that identifies a device or server on a network.
words.example: The computer used an IP address to find the website server.

words.definition: A collection of web pages that people can visit through the internet.
words.example: The class opened a website to look for information.

words.definition: An app used to open websites and web pages.
words.example: A browser can show text, images, links, and videos.

words.definition: A computer that stores or sends information to other computers.
words.example: The website server sent the page to the student's computer.

words.definition: A device or app that asks a server for information.
words.example: The browser acted as a client when it requested the web page.

words.definition: A small piece of data sent across a network.
words.example: A long message can be divided into many packets.

words.definition: The part of a packet that carries delivery information, such as where the packet should go.
words.example: The header helps the network send the packet to the right place.

words.definition: The part of a packet that carries the actual message or data.
words.example: The payload held one piece of the sentence.

words.definition: An agreed rule or method that computers follow to communicate.
words.example: Protocols help devices send data in a way others can understand.

words.definition: A group of connected devices that can share information.
words.example: The school network connects computers to the internet.

words.definition: A device that sends data between networks and helps packets find a path.
words.example: The router moved the packet toward the website server.

words.definition: To move data from one place or device to another.
words.example: The photo transfer took a few seconds.

words.definition: The process of sending data across a connection.
words.example: Packet transmission lets data travel across the internet.

words.definition: The path data takes from one device to another.
words.example: A packet may take a different route from another packet.

words.definition: A worldwide system of connected networks that lets people share information.
words.example: The internet allows students to visit websites and collaborate online.

words.definition: Facts, numbers, text, images, or other information a computer can store or send.
words.example: The computer sent data in packets.

words.definition: The act of getting data to the correct destination.
words.example: The header helps with packet delivery.
